newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Fifth Third CFO on acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Fifth Third CFO on acquisitions.

text.p: Fifth Third Bancorp, which late Thursday said it planned to buy a small competitor, is interested in pursuing larger acquisition targets, its chief financial officer said on Friday.
The Cincinnati-based bank has been rebuffed in some recent attempts, CFO P. Michael Brumm said.
"Some larger (banks) in our general neighborhood would be interesting to us, but they don't seem interested at the moment," Brumm said in a telephone interview.
He said Fifth Third had talked to potential targets in Louisville, Kentucky, and Indianapolis, which both were eventually acquired by other suitors.

"I think we have a reputation as being sort of hard-nosed operators, and that's probably not the most attractive merger partner," he said. "We operate a very no-frills company with a fairly intense culture," where workers arrive early, stay late and don't have perks such as company cars, he said.
Asked if Fifth Third would launch hostile bids, he said, "I think probably not. It would take an unusual set of circumstances."

Brumm said Fifth Third has "historically done a lot of small acquisitions, though it has not made a major acquisition since 1994, when it bought Louisville-based Cumberland Federal Savings, which had assets of about $1.0 billion.
Now, Fifth Third, with 412 banking centers and $20.5 billion in assets, plans to acquire in a stock deal Suburban Bancorp, also in Cincinnati, which has $219 million in assets and seven offices.
AG Edwards & Sons analyst Timothy Willi said the deal was small "but it all adds up. It further enhances Fifth Third's presence in Cincinnati" and brings new customers.
Based on Thursday's stock price, the deal was valued at $32 million, or $20.64 per Suburban share, although the exchange ratio could change with Fifth Third's stock price.
On Friday, Suburban stock closed up 2-3/8 at 19-3/8, while Fifth Third rose 1 to close at 85-3/4 Friday, both on Nasdaq.
Brumm said the price made Fifth Third an unlikely acquisition target, adding a share buyback and other factors may have helped boost the stock from $65 since mid-January.
Analysts said Fifth Third was a sharp operator that successfully integrates acquisitions.
